text:
Dana: quick ask — can someone run a short TCP egress throughput + p95 latency bench on the baremetal private cluster (rack-3) and compare to hosted-prod region? trying to validate a regression we saw in customer X's onprem setup
Marco: yep i can do that. which model & seq length do you want?
Dana: start with rwd-small @ seq=1024 and a longer run for rwd-medium @ seq=2048 if time. primarily care about p95 token latency and tail (99.9). also note NIC offload settings (mtu/jumbo)
Li: pinging infra team — @infra-bot can you provision a short isolated run window on rack-3? need ephemeral access
infra-bot: scheduling job window: rack-3.private 2026-06-05T01:00Z - 2026-06-05T01:20Z. Created ticket INF-8421. Access info: jumpbox at bastion-2 -> sudo on bench user.
Marco: got the window. i'll run with concurrency sweep (4,8,16) and stick to 16 for final. will dump netstat and ethtool info.
Oliver: FYI we saw one case where MTU mismatch (1500 vs 9000) added ~6ms tail on batching. worth checking.
Dana: thanks. include kernel irqbalance status + cpuset pinning details. customer used IRQ affinity to keep NIC interrupts off the GPU CPU cores
Marco: copying my run plan:
```
# on bench host
sudo ethtool -k eth0
sudo ip link show dev eth0
./bench/throughput --model=rwd-small --seq=1024 --concurrency=16 --duration=300 --out=bench-rwd-small-1024.json
# capture perf and tcp stats
sudo perf record -a -g -o perf-rwd-small-1024.data sleep 300
ss -tanm > ss-before.txt; ss -tanm > ss-after.txt
```
I'll upload logs to the ticket when done.
Anya: if you hit NVMe flush stalls, tag me. we had a subtle flush at ~200k tokens/sec on baremetal nodes last quarter.
Marco: first quick numbers (short 60s run) attached below:
```
Model: rwd-small seq=1024 concurrency=16
throughput_tokens/s: 18500
p50_ms: 12.1
p95_ms: 48.7
p99_ms: 86.4
p999_ms: 210.2
```
Hosted-prod (same model) quick run:
```
throughput_tokens/s: 19800
p50_ms: 11.0
p95_ms: 42.3
p99_ms: 76.8
p999_ms: 145.0
```
Marco: so we're seeing ~6ms p95 delta and a larger tail gap (~65ms) on p999. attaching perf samples and a top-like dump.
Priya: could be TCP retransmits on the path — any errors in dmesg or NIC stats?
Marco: ethtool -S shows 0 rx_errors but tx_dropped=12 on eth0; looks small but correlated with p999 spikes.
Dana: that's interesting — customer reported a misconfigured switch buffer earlier. can you re-run with mtu=9000 and mtu=1500 explicitly to compare?
Marco: will do one MTU toggle test in same window. also toggling GRO/TSO off to see change.
Oliver: also check skbuff backlog: cat /proc/net/softnet_stat before/after.
Marco: re-run results (mtu 9000 vs 1500, 300s runs):
```
mtu=9000:
throughput: 19640 tok/s
p95: 41.8 ms
p999: 152.0 ms
mtu=1500:
throughput: 18510 tok/s
p95: 48.5 ms
p999: 215.7 ms
```
Marco: turning off TSO/GSO decreased p999 by ~20ms but reduced throughput ~3%.
Anya: that pattern points at NIC batching adding variability under load — if the GW/TO buffer is small it forces flushes.
Dana: ok next steps: 1) ask infra to check switch buffer settings for rack-3, 2) attempt kernel IRQ affinity changes to separate NIC interrupts from inference CPUs, 3) try a small quantized model run to confirm it's network-specific not compute-bound
Priya: noted. INF-8421 updated with findings + logs. assigning to infra + networking.
Li: thanks everyone. Marco — can you drop the perf.data and the bench jsons into the ticket link when you have a moment?
Marco: done, uploaded perf, bench jsons, ethtool outputs and ss dumps. marking thread as resolved for now unless we see more anomalies. :white_check_mark:
Dana: excellent work — will loop back after infra verifies switch config. (👍)
